name: Knee Cut Passing
description: Use the knee cut with crossface and underhook or long step to beat the knee shield. The knee cut is the highest-percentage guard pass in no-gi BJJ.
shortInstruction: From headquarters, drop your posted knee to the mat, circle it past their knee shield, pin their head with a crossface, and drive to side control.
summary: The knee cut pass attacks the space between the opponent's hip and their near leg as they defend with a knee shield or half guard. The pass works by: (1) pinning their head with a crossface to prevent them from turning into you, (2) driving your near knee past their knee shield into the space at their hip, (3) extending your leg to pin their near hip, and (4) settling into side control. The knee cut is the go-to pass for most no-gi situations because it maintains top pressure throughout and requires minimal space.
whyItWorks: The crossface prevents the opponent from looking away — where the head goes, the body follows
Driving the knee past the knee shield attacks the weakest structural point of their guard — the hip
The knee cut maintains chest-to-chest pressure throughout the pass, preventing them from re-guarding
The knee cut works against all guard types (half guard, deep half, Z-guard, knee shield)
commonMistakes: Cutting the knee without the crossface — the crossface is what prevents their escape, not the knee position
Letting the knee cut stall at the hip — drive through the pass without hesitation
Losing the underhook during the pass — the underhook prevents them from turning into you
Cutting too high (above the hip) instead of below the hip line
coachingCues: Knee past the hip, not above it
safetySummary: The crossface should target the jaw/cheek area, not the throat — throat pressure can cause injury
Do not cut the knee aggressively if your knee is at an awkward angle — this can strain the MCL
If the opponent rolls suddenly during the knee cut, protect your head and follow the roll
keyCorrections: If the knee cut stalls: your crossface is not deep enough — drive the crossface harder to turn their head away
If they roll into you: you lost the underhook — re-pummel the underhook before cutting
If they re-guard after the cut: you released the crossface too early — maintain the crossface through side control

systemLogic.corePrinciple: The knee cut has four phases: Crossface → Knee Entry → Extension → Side Control

decisionTree.action: from headquarters, drive your near arm across their face (jaw/cheek) and pin their head to the mat. This prevents them from turning into you or looking away
drop your posted knee off their hip and drive it past their knee shield. The knee should slide at hip level, not above it
once the knee is past their hip, extend your leg to pin their near hip to the mat. This prevents them from recovering guard
settle into side control with chest-to-chest pressure, underhook, and crossface
standard knee cut (crossface + underhook), long step knee cut (step the far leg over their head to prevent the roll)

moneyDetails: The knee cut is the highest-percentage guard pass in no-gi — it should be your primary pass from headquarters
Mastering the knee cut gives you a reliable path to side control from any open guard
The knee cut to side control scores 3 points in IBJJF (guard pass)
fixItFast: If they keep rolling into the cut: add the long step — step your far leg over their head to block the roll
If they keep shin framing: drop your weight onto the shin to collapse it before cutting
If they keep re-guarding: maintain the crossface through the entire transition to side control
